title: Shadows
sub: Four flags and one shadow map
cards/0/body: Shadows are expensive, so Three.js only draws them when you ask explicitly. You need all four settings:
cards/0/code:
renderer.shadowMap.enabled = true;   // the renderer supports shadows
sun.castShadow = true;               // the light casts shadows
knot.castShadow = true;              // the object casts them
floor.receiveShadow = true;          // the floor receives them
cards/1/task: The sun is shining, but there is no shadow on the floor. Turn on everything it takes.
cards/2/q: You set castShadow on the object and the light, and receiveShadow on the floor, but there is no shadow. What did you forget?
cards/2/options/2: Shadows only work with an OrthographicCamera
cards/2/explain: Without it, the renderer never builds a shadow map at all.
cards/3/body:
The light "photographs" the scene from its own point of view into a depth texture, the shadow map. Then each pixel is checked: can the light see it? If not, it is in shadow.

The map size is light.shadow.mapSize (512×512 by default). Bigger is sharper, but costlier.
cards/4/q: Shadows look jagged and blurry. What do you try first?
cards/4/options/0: Increase light.shadow.mapSize and tighten the shadow camera's area
cards/4/explain: A DirectionalLight renders shadows with an ortho camera, light.shadow.camera. The smaller its box, the sharper the result.
cards/5/q: Which lights can cast shadows? Select all that apply.
cards/5/explain: Ambient shines from everywhere, so there is no side to cast a shadow from. A PointLight renders six maps, which is expensive.
cards/6/q: Match each flag to its meaning
cards/6/pairs/1/1: The light builds a shadow map
cards/7/explain: An object can both cast and receive: set both flags.
